report_name: Polish Power Plant Breached via Private Cellular APN Network

threat_actors.name: Sandworm Team
threat_actors.description: A Russian state-sponsored group, believed to be linked to the FSB, that breached a Polish power plant's industrial network by pivoting through a private cellular network (APN) from a compromised wind farm.

attack_patterns.name: Lateral Tool Transfer
attack_patterns.description: The attackers performed lateral movement from a compromised wind farm into the target power plant's OT network by pivoting through a shared, misconfigured private APN that allowed device-to-device communication.

attack_patterns.name: Remote System Discovery
attack_patterns.description: After pivoting onto the private APN, the attackers scanned the network and discovered a WAGO PFC200 PLC at the combined heat and power (CHP) plant.

attack_patterns.name: Default Credentials
attack_patterns.description: The attackers gained administrative access to a WAGO PFC200 PLC on the OT network by using its default administrator credentials.

attack_patterns.name: Manipulation of Control
attack_patterns.description: Once on the OT network, the attackers issued stop commands to Siemens PLCs, which resulted in the shutdown of a steam turbine and a water treatment system, causing a direct physical impact.

attack_patterns.name: Indicator Removal on Host
attack_patterns.description: The attackers attempted to wipe devices to cover their tracks after the attack, although some forensic evidence was recovered from a router with older firmware.

tools.name: Nmap
tools.description: The use of scanning tools like Nmap was suggested as a hunting hint for detecting anomalous activity on the private APN.

vulnerabilities.name: Private APN Misconfiguration
vulnerabilities.description: A critical misconfiguration in a private Access Point Name (APN) network allowed for device-to-device communication, which enabled attackers to pivot from one compromised entity (a wind farm) to another (a power plant) on the same cellular network.

vulnerabilities.name: Default PLC Credentials
vulnerabilities.description: A WAGO PFC200 PLC was accessible using default administrator credentials, which provided the attackers with immediate administrative access to the OT network upon discovery.

identities.name: Polish Combined Heat and Power Plant
identities.description: A combined heat and power (CHP) plant in Poland that was the primary target of the attack. Its steam turbine and water treatment systems were shut down by the threat actors.

identities.name: Polish Wind Farm
identities.description: The initial point of compromise in the attack campaign. The attackers used its access to a shared private APN to pivot to the main power plant target.

identities.name: FSB
identities.description: Russia's Federal Security Service, which is believed to be linked to the state-sponsored group that conducted the attack.

infrastructure.name: Private Cellular APN
infrastructure.description: A misconfigured private cellular network (APN) provided by a local telecom operator was used as a lateral movement vector, allowing attackers to pivot from a compromised wind farm to the target power plant.

indicators.name: Anomalous East-West Traffic on Private APN
indicators.pattern:
title: Anomalous East-West Traffic on Private APN
id: 7e8b1c2d-9a3b-4f8e-a1d2-c3b4d5e6f7a8
status: experimental
description: >
  Detects network traffic between different end-devices on a private APN. These networks should typically only allow device-to-central-server communication, not peer-to-peer, as seen in the Polish power plant attack.
references:
  - https://thehackernews.com/2026/08/hackers-breach-polish-power-plant.html
author: cyber.netsecops.io
date: 2026-08-11
tags:
  - attack.t0867
  - attack.lateral_movement
level: medium
logsource:
  category: firewall
detection:
  selection:
    src_ip|cidr: '10.0.0.0/8'
    dst_ip|cidr: '10.0.0.0/8'
  filter_known_servers:
    dst_ip:
      - 10.0.0.1 # Placeholder for central management server
  condition: selection and not filter_known_servers
indicators.description: Detects peer-to-peer communication on a private cellular network, which should typically be isolated. This was the key lateral movement vector in the Polish power plant attack.

indicators.name: Nmap Scanning Activity on OT Network
indicators.pattern:
title: Nmap Scanning Activity on OT Network
id: 8f9a2b3c-1d2e-4a9b-8c7d-6f7e8d9c0b1a
status: experimental
description: >
  Detects the execution of Nmap, a network scanning tool, within an OT environment. This was suggested as a hunting hint for detecting discovery activity similar to the Polish power plant attack.
references:
  - https://thehackernews.com/2026/08/hackers-breach-polish-power-plant.html
author: cyber.netsecops.io
date: 2026-08-11
tags:
  - attack.t0846
  - attack.discovery
level: high
logsource:
  category: process_creation
  product: windows
detection:
  selection:
    Image|endswith: '\nmap.exe'
  condition: selection
indicators.description: Detects the use of the Nmap scanning tool, which could indicate an attacker performing discovery on the OT network, as described in the hunting hints for the power plant breach.
